The diagram shown above is the slope field for which of the following differential equations?
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14223512/assets/3673d384035d7febd8540e34143c2a490f7aa3968752785ef809cff16d2524ce.png)

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the slopes of the slope field are horizontal along the lines $x=0$ and $x=2,$ as shown above. Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should evaluate to zero on both of these lines. 

Of the given equations, the only equations that satisfy this condition are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={x}^{2}-2x=x(x-2) \\ {y}^{′} & =2{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}={x}^{2}(2-x)\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, the lines $x=0$ and $x=2$ divide the plane into $3$ regions. The sign of the slopes in each of the $3$ regions are easily deduced by considering the behavior of the solution curves in these regions. This information is summarized in the following table:

| $x<0$ | $0<x<2$ | $x<2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $↗$

$(+)$ | $↘$

$(-)$ | $↗$

$(+)$ |

 
Of the remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}={x}^{2}-2x=x(x-2).
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is ${y}^{′}={x}^{2}-2x.$
